newsitem.title: USA: Big B most active among many deal stocks.
newsitem.headline: Big B most active among many deal stocks.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc's unwelcome $15 per share offer for Big B Inc drew the most attention among Monday's many merger announcements, sparking a 25 percent gain in Big B stock in heavy Nasdaq trade.
Early in Monday's trading session, Big B shares rose as high as 16-1/2 from 12-5/8, a new year-high, before settling back to 15-13/16.
Big B, an Alabama-based drug-store chain, was the Nasdaq market's most active issue, with more than four million shares traded by the second hour of the trading day.
Revco rose 1/4 to 25-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Explaining the stock activity, an arbitrageur said, "You can find values (in previous comparable deals) that are north of 15, plus Big B has no defense, no poison pill and you can throw out the entire Big B board" with a simple majority shareholder vote.
No one at Big B was available for comment.

Also, Revco is very familiar with "drug store deals after the Rite Aid ( Corp) debacle," the arbitrageur said, referring to its $1.8 billion friendly merger proposal that was aborted in April after federal and state regulators opposed the deal on competitive grounds.

Revco -- which operates almost 2,200 drug stores across the United States compared to Big B's 384 stores in the Southeastern U.S. -- said that following the completion of the tender offer, it will offer all remaining Big B shareholders the same cash price paid in the tender offer.
Big B has about 22 million shares on a fully-diluted basis, which values the deal at $330 million, Revco said. Revco now owns 1.19 million Big B shares, or about 5.4 percent of the company.
In another deal announced Monday, Danka Business Systems Plc said it agreed to acquire Eastman Kodak Co's office imaging and facilities management businesses for $648 million in cash.
Danka's Nasdaq-traded American Depositary Receipts rose five points to 34-7/8 after the news, while Kodak slipped 3/8 to 71-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Also, Phar-Mor Inc and ShopKo Stores Inc said they will merge, creating a new company, Cabot Noble Inc.
Phar-Mor shares slid 3/8 to 7-3/4 after the announcement, while ShopKo edged 1/4 higher to 16-1/2.
